headline: Champi now extratropical; Busan markets tour may see rain
summary: Champi has weakened into an extratropical low, reducing the direct tropical-cyclone threat. Rain may affect today's Busan market excursion; rough seas remain possible on the approach and onward sailing. Nagasaki tomorrow is forecast mostly sunny, although residual swell remains possible. No Regent-confirmed itinerary change was identified.

details: Mostly cloudy in Busan, with a shower possible in the morning and periods of rain in the afternoon. Rain timing is uncertain; showers could overlap the 11:00 AM–2:30 PM walking tour.
At approximately 6:35 AM, Busan was 17°C with an easterly wind near 20 km/h. Wear waterproof shoes and carry a rain jacket.
Forecast providers differ on exactly when afternoon showers will occur. Do not treat any one hour as certain.

typhoon.summary: JMA reports Champi became an extratropical low at 9:00 PM JST October 25. KMA's 3:00 AM JST October 26 update places the low in the East China Sea near 31.3°N, 127.5°E at 1000 hPa, moving east-northeast at 20 km/h, with winds around 21 m/s (76 km/h). Rain and waves remain concerns despite loss of typhoon status.
details: JMA's latest typhoon summary issued October 26 at 3:50 AM JST confirms Champi's extratropical transition. The final Champi-specific JMA analysis was issued October 25 at 9:45 PM JST, using 9:00 PM observations: 31.0°N, 126.0°E, 1000 hPa, moving north-northeast 20 km/h.

KMA issued its final Champi advisory October 26 at 3:00 AM JST/KST: extratropical low at 31.3°N, 127.5°E, 1000 hPa, moving east-northeast at 20 km/h. These are different observation times, not conflicting positions.

Change since October 25: the system weakened and transitioned from tropical-storm strength to an extratropical low; its residual wind field and associated front can still produce rough seas and heavy rain.
Busan October 26: rain and potentially rough conditions during approach and departure; a change in port timing or route is possible but not confirmed.
Nagasaki October 27: much drier forecast but lingering swell and wind gusts could affect sailing or shore operations.
Kagoshima October 28 and Beppu October 29: lower direct storm risk; possible knock-on delays if earlier sailing legs change.

Forecast uncertainty remains for exact sea state and localized rainfall. Regent's public itinerary still lists Busan October 26 and Nagasaki October 27; no Regent-confirmed changes were found. Follow onboard announcements.
Typhoon In-fa is near the Marshall Islands at approximately 13.6°N, 164.6°E per JMA's 3:50 AM JST summary and poses no immediate threat to upcoming ports.
